test_cases.Test Description: Verify reset values and masked write/read behavior across GPIO registers. The flow reads each address that is marked as readable and not in the default-skip list, compares the masked value against the documented reset values, then iterates through six data patterns to perform masked writes followed by masked reads and expected-value comparison.
test_cases.Remarks: VRRW-type registers are explicitly skipped per configuration. A noted behavior states that input data tends to read high without external drive; forcing the input low affects bit-level selection and can cause mismatches against expected values.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: the test begins at the primary test routine.

Reset-value verification loop: for each configured address that is not in the default-skip list and is marked readable, perform a register read and apply a mask that clears the least significant bit. Compare the masked value to the documented reset value; on mismatch, record a default-value failure.
Pattern setup: define six 32-bit patterns to exercise register write/read checks.
Write phase per pattern: for each address that is not in the skip list and is marked writable, perform a masked write of the current pattern.

Read/compare phase per pattern: for each address that is not in the skip list and is both writable and readable, perform a masked read. Compute the expected value by combining the written pattern on writable-and-readable bits with the reset value on non-writable-but-readable bits. If the read value does not match the expected value, record a write/read failure.
Completion: if any default-value or write/read failures are recorded, mark the test as failed; otherwise, mark it as passed.

test_cases.Test Description: Configure GPIO pads as inputs with negative-edge interrupt enabled. For each pad, enable its interrupt, generate a falling edge on the corresponding input, and confirm that the pad-level raw status and the group status reflect the event. Then clear the raw status at both pad and group levels and verify clearance while ensuring the input level is low after the falling edge.
test_cases.Remarks: All pads are initially driven high as a known state. Each iteration arms the wait before generating the falling edge and uses a bounded timeout to avoid infinite waits.
Test Steps / Procedure: Entry: the test routine initializes error tracking and enables the interrupt at the CPU controller for the relevant GPIO instance.
Enable system-level routing for the GPIO interrupt source.
Drive the external pad driver register at 0xA0243ffc to all ones to establish a known high level on all pads.

Per-pad configuration loop (32 pads): for each pad register starting at GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 in ascending order, program input mode, enable negative-edge detection, and request raw-clear; wait a short delay after each configuration.
Per-pad test loop: for each pad index, pre-clear its corresponding bit in the group raw-status-clear register.
Enable only the current pad’s interrupt in the group enable register; wait a short delay.
Arm the wait condition for the interrupt service to signal completion.
Generate a falling edge for the current pad by first driving all pads high, waiting briefly, then driving the external pad driver such that only the current pad is low.
Wait for the interrupt with a bounded timeout; if the timeout expires, record an error for this pad and proceed.
In the interrupt service, return the external pad driver to the known high state, then read the current pad’s register.
Verify that the input state bit indicates a low level following the falling edge; on mismatch, record an error.
Confirm that the group interrupt status register shows the bit corresponding to the current pad; if not set, record an error.
Clear the pad-level raw status by writing the pad register with input mode and the raw-clear request, and also clear the group raw status bit using the group raw-status-clear register.
Verify that the group interrupt status register reads zero after clearing; on mismatch, record an error.
Clear the system-level interrupt latch and the CPU controller pending state for the relevant interrupt source.
Upon completion of all iterations, finish the test with pass if no errors were recorded.
